target.title: fix(telegram): polling worker pins a CPU core when the Bot API answers empty getUpdates instantly
target.body:
Closes #111062

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running the Telegram channel in polling mode against a Bot API endpoint that answers `getUpdates` immediately — notably self-hosted `telegram-bot-api` servers and some intermediary proxies — would see the ingress worker busy-spin while the chat is idle: each empty poll completes in milliseconds and the next one starts right away, pinning a CPU core and flooding the endpoint with requests. Observed in production on 2026-05-22 with a self-hosted `telegram-bot-api` server that did not hold the requested long-poll timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The polling loop trusted the endpoint to enforce the requested long-poll timeout and had no pacing of its own. This change enforces a 1-second floor between consecutive empty `getUpdates` cycles, measured from poll start, so endpoints that honor the long-poll timeout are never delayed and non-empty polls still drain pending traffic at full speed. The wait listens to the worker stop signal, so shutdown stays immediate; error paths keep their existing backoff and `retry_after` behavior.

## User Impact

Telegram polling against fast-answering Bot API endpoints now idles at near-zero CPU instead of pinning a core. Update delivery latency is unchanged for endpoints that honor the long-poll timeout and for busy chats; the worst case for a fast-empty endpoint is one poll per second while idle.

## Evidence

- Production incident (2026-05-22): a gateway polling a self-hosted `telegram-bot-api` server spun the ingress worker at ~100% CPU while idle because the endpoint returned empty `getUpdates` responses immediately instead of holding the long poll. The same pacing, applied as a local patch, removed the spin without affecting delivery latency.
- New regression test in `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.test.ts` ("paces fast successful empty getUpdates responses") proves with fake timers that after an instant empty response the next poll does not start at 999 ms and starts exactly at the 1000 ms floor.
- Existing worker tests (durable-before-offset, retry policy) still pass, proving non-empty polls and error/backoff paths are unchanged: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.test.ts` — 8/8 passed; `extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.test.ts` — 75/75 passed.

This fix was developed with AI assistance; the change and its validation were reviewed by the submitting author.


## Runtime evidence (added after ClawSweeper review)

### Runtime proof: paced empty polling vs `origin/main`

**Harness.** A small Node HTTP server implements a minimal controlled Bot API endpoint: `POST /bot<token>/getUpdates` answers immediately with `{"ok":true,"result":[]}`, logging every request with a monotonic millisecond timestamp — modeling an endpoint or proxy that returns before the requested long-poll timeout. A driver runs the real `runTelegramIngressWorkerRuntime` poll loop from this branch against that endpoint with the production transport path (undici HTTP/1.1 dispatcher) and real timers — no fake clocks — for 10 seconds, then sends the worker `stop` command and measures time to exit. The BEFORE run executes a byte-identical copy of `origin/main`'s `telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.ts` (git blob `4246d45066`) through the same driver and endpoint; this branch changes no sibling module, so the baseline behaves exactly as `main`.

**Repro** (from a branch checkout; the throwaway harness — an ~85-line fake Bot API server plus an ~80-line driver in a local `.proof/` directory — is intentionally not part of the PR):

```sh
# AFTER (this branch)
node_modules/.bin/tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.json .proof/driver.mts
# BEFORE (origin/main poll loop, same driver and endpoint)
git show origin/main:extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.ts \
  > extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.main-baseline.ts
POLL_FLOOR_RUNTIME_MODULE=$PWD/extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.main-baseline.ts \
  node_modules/.bin/tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.json .proof/driver.mts
```

**BEFORE — `origin/main` loop spins: 4,800 empty polls in 10 s (~480/s).** Excerpt (checkout prefix redacted; server live-logs the first 25 requests, then every 1,000th; every request is counted):

```text

[driver] controlled fast-empty Bot API listening on 127.0.0.1:45537
[driver] running real poll loop for 10s, then sending stop
[bot-api] +    55ms getUpdates #1 (timeout=30, offset=none) -> {"ok":true,"result":[]}
[bot-api] +    74ms getUpdates #2 (timeout=30, offset=none) -> {"ok":true,"result":[]}
[bot-api] +    79ms getUpdates #3 (timeout=30, offset=none) -> {"ok":true,"result":[]}
...
[bot-api] +  2342ms getUpdates #1000 (timeout=30, offset=none) -> {"ok":true,"result":[]}
[bot-api] +  4549ms getUpdates #2000 (timeout=30, offset=none) -> {"ok":true,"result":[]}
[bot-api] +  6605ms getUpdates #3000 (timeout=30, offset=none) -> {"ok":true,"result":[]}
[bot-api] +  8548ms getUpdates #4000 (timeout=30, offset=none) -> {"ok":true,"result":[]}
[driver] +10036ms sending stop signal (poll-success messages so far: 4800)
[driver] +10044ms poll loop exited 9ms after stop signal
[bot-api] summary: 4800 empty getUpdates responses over 10.0s (~480.7 polls/sec)
[bot-api] per-second request counts: s0=392 s1=460 s2=445 s3=463 s4=449 s5=508 s6=452 s7=535 s8=535 s9=540 s10=21
```

**AFTER — branch loop paces to one empty poll per second and still stops promptly.** Full request log (checkout prefix redacted). The stop signal landed mid-pacing-sleep (last poll at +9062 ms, stop at +10045 ms) and the abort woke the sleep immediately — exit 6 ms after stop:

